content.title: Celtics-Heat recap: Historic first quarter propels C's to wild win
content.text: Boston CelticsLive Blog EndedApr 1, 2026 The Celtics scored 53 points in the first quarter of their 147-129 win. NBC Universal, Inc. Sam Hauser caught up with Abby Chin after the C’s wild win over Miami What to KnowChris Forsberg and Kayla Burton shared more postgame reaction on the Celtics Talk Podcast.Celtics scored 53 points and shot 11-of-15 from 3 in the first quarter.Jaylen Brown dropped a game-high 43 points (17-29 FG).Jayson Tatum recorded his first triple-double since Feb. 2025.Sam Hauser scored 23 points with five 3-pointers. The Boston Celtics completed a 4-0 season sweep of the Miami Heat with an emphatic road win on Wednesday night, 147-129. Boston set the tone with a historic 53-point first quarter. Miami later responded with a 45-point third quarter, but the C's pulled away again in the fourth to secure the statement win against a potential first-round opponent. Jaylen Brown dropped a game-high 43 points in the win. Jayson Tatum added 25 points, 18 rebounds, and 11 assists for his first triple-double since Feb, 2025. Check out our live blog below for a full recap of Wednesday's game: The Boston Celtics scored 53 points in the first quarter and didn't look back as they dominated the Miami Heat in Wednesday night's showdown at Kaseya Center, 147-129. Boston shot 20-of-28 from the field and 11-of-15 from 3-point range in its historic opening frame. The team's 53 points marked the most it has ever scored in a first quarter and tied for the second-most first-quarter points in NBA history. The C's led the rest of the way, though the Heat briefly made it interesting by cutting its 27-point deficit to single digits early in the fourth quarter. Miami scored 45 points and matched Boston's first-quarter 3-point shooting (11-15 3-PT) in the third. Celtics superstars Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum assured that Boston wouldn't relinquish its lead. The Jays combined for 68 points, 21 rebounds, and 18 assists. They scored or assisted on 105 of Boston's 147 points, per ESPN Insights. Jayson Tatum grabbed 39.5 percent of available defensive rebounds vs. Miami. He's at 25.2 percent for the season, which is 5 percent higher than the next-closest wing (Josh Hart, 20.2 percent). Only players with a better rate this season, per Cleaning the Glass: Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic, Jusuf Nurkic, Domantas Sabonis, Karl-Anthony Towns, Kevin Love, Andre Drummond. Top 20 are all bigs beyond Tatum. Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown were the stars of the show Wednesday night, combining for 68 points, 21 rebounds, and 18 assists while scoring or assisting on a whopping 71 percent of Boston's 147 points. After the game, both superstars showed the other some love for their impact on winning. Our Celtics Postgame Live crew shares its immediate reaction to Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum leading Boston to a dominant win over the Heat: Sam Hauser scored 23 points on 5-of-7 shooting from 3-point range in Miami. All five 3s came in the first quarter. After the win, he caught up with NBC Sports Boston's Abby Chin to talk about his big night: Sam Hauser caught up with Abby Chin after the C's wild win over Miami Score: 139-122 Celtics, 2:43 left in fourth quarter This one is all but over as the Celtics are up 17 with just under three minutes left in regulation. Boston has outscored Miami 27-20 in the fourth, bouncing back from its poor defensive third. Score: 121-105 Celtics, 9:36 left in fourth quarter The Heat shot 11-of-15 from 3-point range in the third quarter to get back into the game, then they cut the deficit to single digits at the start of the fourth quarter. The C's quickly responded, however, going on a 7-0 run to go back up by 16. Jayson Tatum officially has a triple-double with 22 points, 14 rebounds, and 10 assists. It's his first triple-double since Feb. 20, 2025. Score: 112-102 Celtics The Heat have cut a 27-point deficit to 10 with a strong third quarter in which they made 11 3-pointers. They outscored the Celtics 45-32 in the frame. Jaime Jaquez Jr. has provided Miami with a spark off the bench, scoring 13 points and nailing a pair of 3s in the quarter. Davion Mitchell (17 points) also hit a couple of 3s, including a buzzer-beater at the end of the quarter. All five Heat starters are in double figures, including Bam Adebayo with a team-leading 21 points. Jaylen Brown leads all scorers with 36 points, marking his 34th 30-point performance of the season. Jayson Tatum is on the brink of a triple-double with 17 points, 14 rebounds, and nine assists. Score: 101-77 Celtics, 4:55 left in third quarter The Celtics have passed the 100-point threshold, and we still have five minutes left in the third quarter. Jaylen Brown has led the way with 36 points, while Sam Hauser has added 19 on 5-of-7 shooting from 3-point range. Jayson Tatum has a double-double with 17 points and 13 rebounds. Score: 95-77 Celtics, 6:56 left in third quarter The Heat have outscored the C's 20-15 so far in the third, but Boston still has a comfortable 18-point lead. Jaylen Brown has been outstanding for the Celtics, scoring a game-high 32 points on 12-of-19 shooting. It's his 34th 3-point game of the season, marking the third-most in the NBA and most in the Eastern Conference. Legendary Patriots quarterback Tom Brady is courtside in Miami to take in the Celtics-Heat action: Score: 80-57 Celtics The Celtics are up big on the Heat after a historic first half in Miami. Boston erupted for 53 points in the first quarter, the most they've ever scored in an opening quarter and tied for the second-most first-quarter points in NBA history. The Heat held the C's to 27 points in the second quarter, but Boston still outscored Miami 27-23 in the frame to widen its lead to 21. Score: 70-51 Celtics, 4:37 left in second quarter Boston is up to 70 points with just under five minutes still to go in the first half, and it's because of its sharpshooting from beyond the arc. The Celtics are shooting 14-of-22 from 3-point range, tying their season-high for 3s made in a half. Sam Hauser (17 points) and Jayson Tatum (11 points) are a combined 8-for-11 from deep. Score: 61-42 Celtics, 8:13 left in second quarter The Celtics' 53 points marked the most they've ever scored in a first quarter and are tied for the second-most first-quarter points in NBA history. Jaylen Brown's 20 points are tied for the second most he's ever scored in a first quarter. Sam Hauser's 17 points marked a first-quarter career-high, and his five 3-pointers tied a Celtic record (via Celtics stats guru Dick Lipe). As for the second quarter, the C's took a timeout after a 6-0 Heat run. Score: 53-33 Celtics The first quarter couldn't have gone much better for the Celtics, who scored a season-high 53 points in the frame. Boston was unstoppable offensively, shooting 20-of-28 from the floor and 11-of-15 from 3-point range. Jaylen Brown notched 20 points (the most he has scored in a quarter this season) on 8-of-11 shooting from the field, while Sam Hauser added 17 points on 5-of-5 shooting from beyond the arc, tying his season-high for 3s in a quarter. Bam Adebayo led the Heat with 11 points. Miami shot 6-of-12 from 3-point range, but just 9-of-24 from the field. Score: 39-30 Celtics, 2:41 left in first quarter The Celtics are up to 39 points and we still have just under three minutes left in the opening frame. Jaylen Brown has led the charge with a game-high 17 points on 7-of-9 shooting. Sam Hauser has also made an impact with 11 points on 4-of-4 from the floor (3-3 3-PT). Boston is shooting a ridiculous 15-for-20 from the field and 7-of-8 from beyond the arc. All five C's players who have attempted a 3-pointer have made at least one. Score: 21-21, 6:31 left in first quarter It has been an entertaining opening quarter in Miami with both teams scoring at will. Jaylen Brown has done most of the damage so far for the Celtics. He scored Boston's first 11 points and has 13 (5-6 FG) through five minutes. Sam Hauser and Jayson Tatum have chipped in five and three points, respectively. For the Heat, Bam Adebayo has gone toe-to-toe with Brown with 11 points. Celtics: Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Sam Hauser, Jayson Tatum, Neemias Queta Heat: Davion Mitchell, Tyler Herro, Pelle Larson, Andrew Wiggins, Bam Adebayo Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown are ready for Wednesday's showdown against the Heat. Tatum is back after missing Monday's loss in Atlanta. The Celtics and Heat could meet again in the first round of the playoffs. Before Wednesday's game, Heat coach Erik Spoelstra spoke about the historic rivalry between the two Eastern Conference foes: "I mean, it's not going anywhere," he said. "I know they're probably looking at us -- they're second in the East. They were where they were the year before. So, they're probably looking at us the way they should. They don't see us as a threat. We need to play better. We understand that, we understand where we are, understand what's happened. "We're not oblivious to things. We're not oblivious to what's happening. In three games with them, they've earned those games. Each of those fourth quarters. Tonight's another opportunity for us to change that." Celtics Nikola Vucevic (finger) - OUT Heat Norman Powell (illness) - OUT Terry Rozier (not injury related) - OUT Jayson Tatum talks about Nikola Vucevic’s progress as he rehabs from a fractured finger. Nikola Vucevic was acquired by the Boston Celtics before the Feb. 6 NBA trade deadline and played 12 games for his new team before suffering a fractured finger injury that required surgery. Vucevic has been working hard to get back on the court, although the team hasn't announced an official return date for him. With just eight games left in the regular season, time is running out for the veteran center to build more chemistry with his new teammates before the playoffs. "Vooch has been working his ass off. He'll be back soon, I hope," Tatum told reporters at shootaround ahead of Wednesday night's game against the Heat in Miami. What kind of impact could Vucevic have for the Celtics in the playoffs? There are 13 days left in the NBA’s 2025-26 regular season, but the Eastern Conference playoff picture remains a chaotic blur with the six teams in spots 5-10 separated by just 3.5 games. Trying to predict who might emerge as the Boston Celtics’ first-round opponent remains a dart throw. Here’s what we know: The Celtics hold a two-game lead on the Knicks in the race for the No. 2 seed, though New York holds the head-to-head tiebreaker (division record) if the teams finish with matching records. There’s a very good chance that the final head-to-head meeting on April 9 will dictate exactly who emerges with the No. 2 seed. The finish line of the Celtics’ schedule feels a bit like a playoff appetizer platter. Seven of Boston’s final 10 games are against potential first-round opponents, or that cluster of six teams slotted in spots 5-10 in the East. The Knicks would be the Round 2 opponent if they stay at No. 3 and the higher seeds take care of business in Round 1. Given the volatility in spots 5-10, we wondered if there are more agreeable opponents than others for the Celtics. If Boston finishes with the No. 2 seed, it would play the winner of the 7-8 play-in game in Round 1; if the Celtics finish with the No. 3 seed, they would play the No. 6 seed to start the playoffs.
